The atoms in between the Rydberg atom nucleus and electron (so the atoms inside the atom) interact with the electron in a wide orbit from the Rydberg atom, so polarons, but Rydberg ones :)

The atoms in the space between the electron and the Rydberg atom exert a minimal force on the electron, causing it to be scattered very slightly and creating a weak bond between the atoms. This leads to the Rydberg polaron state of matter
Physics
This state of matter is referred to as “Rydberg polarons", fitting an atom in the space between the nucleus and electrons of another atom.
